request.title: Prove Printed.modulatedExponentialDecay_bounded_iff_countable_twists_false (Proposition D.3.3.10(3), p. 807)
request.body:
Proves the refutation of the printed countable boundedness test, Proposition D.3.3.10(3), p. 807 (ERRATA F12).

Closes #4657

**Counterexample** (`Printed.modulatedExponentialDecay_bounded_iff_countable_twists_false`): G = ℝ≥0ˣ with identity modulation and section, I = [0,1], J = {1/(k+2)} ∪ {1 − 1/(k+2)} (countable; accumulates at both endpoints in EReal, and every exponent in J is < 1). B is the image under `identityModulationExponentialDecay_equiv` of the log profiles `fₙ(x) = exp(−n) ψ(x − n)`, with ψ a `ContDiffBump` at 0 (radii 1/2, 1).

- For a < 1 the a-twist of fₙ is `exp(−(1−a)n) · h(x − n)` with h the twist of f₀. Each Schwartz seminorm (k, l) of it is at most `k! eᶜ / cᵏ · 2ᵏ · sup_{≤(k,l)} p(h)` with c = 1 − a, so the twisted family is bounded; it is carried to `SchwartzBruhat ℝ≥0ˣ` by the log-coordinate equivalence `schwartzBruhat_realCoordinate_equiv` (private in Sec3a, reached with `import all`).
- The 1-twist of fₙ equals 1 at x = n, so its seminorm (1, 0) is at least n; hence {fₙ} is unbounded in `PositiveRealExponentialDecay [0,1]`, and B is unbounded.

The docstring of the refutation is updated to name the J actually used (the paper's choice, the rationals in (0,1), would work the same way). Helpers are `private theorem`s directly above it; imports added: `import all RiemannMasullo.AppD_SchwartzBruhat.Sec3a`, `Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.InnerProduct`. No statement changed.

**Checks run**
- `lake build RiemannMasullo.AppD_SchwartzBruhat.Sec3a_part2_Printed`: ok, the module builds in about 5 s.
- `lake build` (full): ok.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: ok.
- Signatures of the module before/after (`lake env lean --run scripts/Signatures.lean RiemannMasullo.AppD_SchwartzBruhat.Sec3a_part2_Printed`, then `scripts/signatures.sh --compare`): no changes.
- `#print axioms RiemannMasullo.Printed.modulatedExponentialDecay_bounded_iff_countable_twists_false`: `[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The `sorryAx` comes from library lemmas still open upstream: `identityModulationExponentialDecay_equiv` and `schwartzBruhat_realCoordinate_equiv` both show `sorryAx` on `main`.
